pages.title: Learn a threshold neuron from mistakes
pages.subtitle: Lecture 3, PDF page 41: labels are +1 and -1, with a unit-size update.
blocks: Original study data, always visited in this order: A = (1,0), target +1; B = (0,1), target -1; C = (1,1), target +1.
The leading 1 is a bookkeeping input for the bias. It is not another measured feature.
The slide does not define sign(0). We choose +1 explicitly. These labels differ from the 0/1 labels used in logistic regression.

pages.title: Update only after a mistaken prediction
pages.subtitle: An epoch is one complete pass through A, B, C in that order.
blocks: Use the newest weights for the very next example. The update is not a batch average and does not wait until the epoch ends.
Stop only after an entire epoch has no classification errors. With our tie rule, score zero is correct for target +1 and incorrect for target -1.

pages.title: Why the mistake update helps this point
pages.subtitle: Examine the first mistaken visit: B in epoch 1.
blocks: Squared length means the sum of squared components. The score moves downward toward the negative target. A positive target moves its own score upward. Other points can become wrong again, which is why we repeat epochs.
Do not replace the mistake test by y times score <= 0 under this tie convention: a zero score with target +1 is already correct.

pages.title: Verify the final neuron and stop
pages.subtitle: The fourth epoch has zero errors; the third still had one.
blocks: Five updates occurred over twelve visits. A visit, a mistake update and an epoch are different counts.

pages.title: Picture the final separating boundary
pages.subtitle: Points on the line receive +1 because sign(0) = +1.
blocks: The boundary is 2x1 - x2 - 1 = 0. C lies exactly on it; our tie convention matters.
Lecture 3, pages 53-54: a single perceptron cannot solve nonseparable data such as XOR. Repeating the loop then need not produce an error-free epoch.

pages.title: Your turn: two points, one measured feature
pages.subtitle: Keep +1/-1 labels, sign(0) = +1 and the unit mistake update.
blocks: Fixed order: first x = -1 with target -1; then x = 2 with target +1.
Show the old weights, score, predicted label and resulting weights for every visit. Repeat until a complete epoch has no errors.
How many visits, mistake updates and epochs are required? Explain why the first epoch alone is not enough.

pages.title: Practice answer: correct both first-epoch errors
pages.subtitle: The second point uses the weights already changed by the first.
blocks: Both visits made an update. Even though the final weights may now be correct, the stopping rule requires another complete pass.

pages.title: Practice answer: check the whole second epoch
pages.subtitle: The first correct point is not yet an error-free epoch.
blocks: Now stop: 2 epochs, 4 visits, 2 mistake updates. Remember to update the bias, preserve visit order, and distinguish a score from its predicted label.
